description:
Extends the fault catalog to whole nodes, at low weight relative to process kills.

- Node halt, abrupt and graceful.
- Node halt followed by restart against the SAME data directory, which exercises recovery-from-disk rather than fresh bootstrap. bedrock_ex's dev.exs was configured specifically for this (a stable data_dir so restarts exercise recovery) and it is where cross-node worker init failures showed up.

Two things the spike established that this child must respect: object storage is shared across all nodes (per-node stores produce N isolated clusters that never converge, and it fails as a timeout rather than an error), and a restarted node must rejoin the existing cluster rather than fall back to a single-node descriptor -- which the descriptor fallback (bedrock-y3c) makes disturbingly easy to do silently.

Liveness oracle earns its keep here: after faults stop, the cluster must serve transactions again within a bounded time. Wedged recovery and epoch thrash are the expected failure modes.
title: Node-level faults: halt and restart-from-disk
